tone_statements.quote: The Kuroshima dialect of Yaeyama, Southern Ryukyuan, has a three-pattern accent system with three contrasting accent types (a, b, and c). Previous studies have indicated a clear contrast between the three accent types for simplex and compound nouns in Kuroshima. However, despite conducting several investigations using the same methodology as previous studies, we could not identify the contrast between types a and b for simplex nouns, although we successfully identified three contrasting types for compound nouns.

tone_statements.quote: 本稿では以上の点を踏まえ，二型アクセント体系を持つとされてきた八重山語の4つの方言（大浜，宮良，石垣四箇，西表古見）を取り上げ，これらの方言では，①3つのアクセント型が区別されており，②「韻律語」という韻律単位（五十嵐2015，2016）が機能しているという2点を明らかにする。
tone_statements.translation: Taking these points into account, this paper takes up four dialects of Yaeyama that have been said to have a two-pattern accent system (Ohama, Miyara, Ishigaki-Shika, Iriomote-Komi) and shows two things: (1) three accent types are distinguished in these dialects, and (2) a prosodic unit called the 'prosodic word' (Igarashi 2015, 2016) is at work.

Nihon Hōgen Kenkyūkai Kenkyū Happyōkai Happyō Genkōshū 日本方言研究会研究発表会発表原稿集 (Conference Papers of the Dialectological Circle of Japan) 118: 33–40.
tone_statements.quote: 以上の結果に基づき、船浮方言のアクセント体系を次のように記述できる。第一に、音節より上位、文節より下位の韻律語という単位を有しており、b 型と c 型の場合、この単位が数える単位として機能している。第二に、アクセント型によって指定されているピッチの変動は音節を単位として実現している。第三に、局所的なピッチの変動（上昇）の有無と位置によって 4 つのアクセント型が対立する。船浮の体系の概要を表 6 に示す。祖納と干立について同じ解釈を採用できる。網取は、固定型が殆ど確認されないため、a 型、b 型、c 型の三型アクセント体系を有すると解釈する。
tone_statements.translation: Based on the above results, the accent system of the Funauki dialect can be described as follows. First, it has a unit, the prosodic word, above the syllable and below the bunsetsu, and for types b and c this unit functions as the counting unit. Second, the pitch movement specified by the accent type is realised with the syllable as its unit. Third, four accent types contrast by the presence/absence and position of a local pitch movement (rise). Table 6 outlines the Funauki system. The same interpretation can be adopted for Sonai and Hoshitate. For Amitori, since the kotei type is hardly attested, we interpret it as having a three-pattern accent system of types a, b, c.

tone_statements.summary: N-pattern word accent: 4 accent types in Funauki/Sonai/Hoshitate (3 in simple nouns, 4 in compounds), 3 in Amitori; prosodic word is the counting unit; kotei type from tonogenesis. forms: at least.

tone_statements.quote: 秋永 (1960)、平山ほか (1967) の研究以降、大浜方言では少なくとも 2 つのアクセント型（下降型、平板型）が対立することが知られているが、大浜方言のアクセント体系を詳細に記述した研究は未だに実現していない。…現時点での調査資料の分析に基づき、現代大浜方言も先行研究で記述されている通り、下降型と平板型のアクセント型を区別しているという結果が得られた。あわせて、470語についてそのアクセント型の所属情報を報告する。

tone_statements.citation: Celik, Kenan, Reiko Aso & Kōhei Nakazawa セリック ケナン・麻生玲子・中澤光平. 2022. Minami Ryūkyū Yaeyama-go Miyara hōgen no meishi akusento shiryō 南琉球八重山語宮良方言の名詞アクセント資料 [Report on the lexical prosodic system of nouns in the Southern Ryukyuan Yaeyama Miyara dialect]. NINJAL Research Papers 国立国語研究所論集 22: 157–176.
tone_statements.quote: 第一に，先行研究の記述の通り，単純名詞は2つのアクセント型（下降型・平板型）が区別される。第二に，2つの名詞から成る複合語の大部分においては複合語全体の音調が前部要素のアクセント型で決まっており，いわゆる「複合アクセント法則」が成立している。ただし，少数の複合語においては異なるパターンも観察される。第三に，下降型の単純名詞は琉球祖語のA系列に，平板型の名詞はBC系列に所属するという規則的な対応関係が見出される。
tone_statements.translation: First, as described in previous studies, simplex nouns distinguish two accent types (falling and flat). Second, in most compounds of two nouns the pitch pattern of the whole compound is determined by the accent type of the first member, i.e. the 'compound accent law' holds, though a few compounds show other patterns. Third, a regular correspondence is found: falling-type simplex nouns belong to Proto-Ryukyuan class A and flat-type nouns to classes B/C.

tone_statements.n_tones: 2 accent types in simplex nouns (falling 下降型, flat 平板型)

tone_statements.citation: Urabe, Yuko (2022). Shiraho (Okinawa, Southern Ryukyuan). In An Introduction to the Japonic Languages. Leiden: Brill. pp. 155-187.
tone_statements.quote: Shiraho has a three-pattern pitch accent system that is determined lexically (Nakagawa and Celik 2019). The accent patterns are shown in figures 6.2, 6.3, and 6.4. Falling-1 is a steep falling pattern in which pitch falls around the second syllable. Falling-2 is a slightly falling pattern in which the pitch falls around the second syllable, but the degree of fall in pitch is lower than Falling-1. The level pattern keeps a high pitch. According to Nakagawa and Celik (2019), the falling-2 and level patterns are in complementary distribution ... In compound nouns, the tonal pattern is determined by that of the first constituent.
tone_statements.summary: Three lexical accent patterns (Falling-1, Falling-2, Level) shown with pitch tracks in Hz; Falling-2/Level complementary by onset voicing; compounds take first member's pattern; pitch marks aspect.

tone_statements.citation: Aso, Reiko (2020). Minami Ryūkyū Yaeyamago Hateruma Hōgen no Bunpō. Tokyo University of Foreign Studies.
tone_statements.quote: 波照間方言は、ピッチの高低が弁別的な三型アクセント体系を有する。その 3 つとは、下降型、平進型、上昇型である。単一のアクセントがかかるドメインは、語、あるいは語と接語である。... 下降型：アクセント単位末尾に向けて下降する。... 平進型：下降も上昇もしない。... 上昇型：アクセント単位末尾に向けて上昇する。... 図に示す通り、アクセント単位の長さが変わってもアクセント型の対立が一定であり、上昇あるいは下降の位置、すなわちどの音節あるいはモーラでピッチが変動するかは、非弁別的である。そのため、N 型アクセント (上野 1977, 2012) でかつ語声調 (早田 1977, 1999) の言語であると言える。
tone_statements.translation: The Hateruma dialect has a three-pattern accent system in which pitch height is distinctive. The three are the falling type, the level type and the rising type. The domain over which a single accent applies is the word, or the word plus clitic. ... Falling type: falls toward the end of the accent unit. ... Level type: neither falls nor rises. ... Rising type: rises toward the end of the accent unit. ... As the figures show, the opposition of accent types stays constant even when the length of the accent unit changes, and the position of the rise or fall, i.e. on which syllable or mora the pitch changes, is non-distinctive. It can therefore be said to be an N-pattern accent (Uwano 1977, 2012) and word-tone (Hayata 1977, 1999) language.
tone_statements.locator: pp. 50-51, §2.3 アクセント; footnote callouts 28-30 and the tone-letter notation omitted at the elisions
tone_statements.summary: Three word-level melodies (falling, level, rising) written with IPA tone letters after the accent unit; author terms it N-pattern accent and word tone, not Tokyo-type pitch accent; Praat F0 figures.

tone_statements.citation: Shimabukuro, Moriyo 島袋盛世. 2016. Hateruma sogo meishi akusento taikei no saiken 波照間祖語名詞アクセント体系の再建 [A Reconstruction of Hateruma Noun Accent]. Ryūdai Review of Euro-American Studies 琉球大学欧米文化論集 60: 1–22. Nishihara: University of the Ryukyus (法文学部国際言語文化学科 欧米系). [in Japanese] doi:10.24564/0002008382, hdl:20.500.12000/34845.
tone_statements.quote: 本論文は波照間島の北集落と南集落で話されている2つの方言のアクセントを比較し，波照間祖語の2モーラ及び3モーラ名調アクセント体系の再建を試みる。さらに，再建された祖語体系から北集落及び南集落方言のアクセント体系へ変化していった過程を説明する。基礎語彙のアクセントデータは主に，平山・中本(1964)，平山・大島・中本(1967)，崎村(1987，2006)を用いる。祖語のアクセント体系は，北・南集落方言アクセントの規則的な対応関係に基づくと，2モーラ，3モーラ名詞両方とも4つの型が再建できる。
tone_statements.translation: This paper compares the accent of the two dialects spoken in the northern and southern settlements of Hateruma Island and attempts a reconstruction of the Proto-Hateruma accent system of 2-mora and 3-mora nouns ['名調' sic for 名詞]. It further explains the process of change from the reconstructed proto-system to the accent systems of the northern- and southern-settlement dialects. The accent data for basic vocabulary are mainly taken from Hirayama & Nakamoto (1964), Hirayama, Oshima & Nakamoto (1967) and Sakimura (1987, 2006). Based on the regular correspondences between the northern and southern settlement accents, four types can be reconstructed for both 2-mora and 3-mora nouns in the proto-system.

tone_statements.n_tones: 4 reconstructed accent classes for 2-mora and for 3-mora nouns in Proto-Haterum…

Nihon Joshi Daigaku Kiyō Bungakubu 日本女子大学紀要 文学部 (Journal, Faculty of Humanities, Japan Women's University) 64: 55–92. [in Japanese; no DOI on the record]
tone_statements.quote: このようにして、この黒島方言も三型アクセント体系を持つことが判明した。...（32）黒島方言アクセントの仕組み （a）その体系内の３種の型のアクセントは、ピッチの下降の有無とその位置の違いによって区別される。（b）それぞれの型のアクセントは、次のように出現する。〈ａ型〉下がり目がない 〈ｂ型〉２つめの韻律語（PW）に出現 〈ｃ型〉最初の韻律語（PW）に出現 （c）下降は、原則的にそれぞれのPWの次末モーラに出現する。...（33）黒島方言の音調付与規則 （a）Ｈ音調付与規則 韻律句の最初のモーラから、アクセントのあるモーラまでを高くする。（b）Ｌ音調付与規則 アクセントを持つモーラの直後のモーラから、韻律句の最後のモーラまでを低くする。
tone_statements.translation: In this way it became clear that the Kuroshima dialect too has a three-pattern accent system. ... (32) Mechanism of Kuroshima accent: (a) the accents of the three types in the system are distinguished by the presence or absence of a pitch fall and by its position. (b) The accent of each type appears as follows: type a, no fall; type b, in the second prosodic word (PW); type c, in the first prosodic word (PW). (c) The fall appears in principle on the penultimate mora of the respective PW. ... (33) Tone-assignment rules of Kuroshima: (a) H-tone rule: make high from the first mora of the prosodic phrase up to the accented mora. (b) L-tone rule: make low from the mora right after the accented mora to the last mora of the prosodic phrase.
tone_statements.summary: Three lexical accent classes (a/b/c) realised as the place of a pitch fall counted over prosodic words; Kohama: rising kernel; Hateruma tentatively 4 types (a,b,c + fall-rise x). 30+ marked forms.

tone_statements.citation: Harada, Soichiro (2015). Minami Ryūkyū Yaeyama-Kuroshima no bunpō. Osaka University. 284 pp.
tone_statements.quote: 黒島方言は 2 つのアクセントパターンを持つ。1 つ目は、領域末に下降があるパターンで、もう 1 つは下降がないパターンである。... アクセント付与規則がかかる領域は、語＋助詞（次章で述べる「助詞付き名詞句」）である。下降を含むパターンの場合、この領域内の末尾のモーラが低くなる。下降のないパターンでは、末尾まで高く発音される。... 以下にそれぞれのパターンの例を示す。L は低い実現を、H は高い実現を意味する。(2-62) 下降を含むパターン ： /par/ HL「針」 /pannudu/ LHHL「針が」 下降を含まないパターン ： /tur/ LH 「鳥」 /tunnudu/ LHHH「鳥が」
tone_statements.translation: The Kuroshima dialect has two accent patterns. The first is a pattern with a fall at the end of the domain, the other a pattern with no fall. ... The domain to which the accent assignment rule applies is word + particle (the 'noun phrase with particle' of the next chapter). In the pattern containing a fall, the final mora within this domain becomes low. In the pattern without a fall, it is pronounced high to the end. ... Examples of each pattern follow. L means a low realisation, H a high realisation. (2-62) pattern with fall: /par/ HL 'needle', /pannudu/ LHHL 'needle-NOM'; pattern without fall: /tur/ LH 'bird', /tunnudu/ LHHH 'bird-NOM'.
tone_statements.summary: Two-pattern word accent (falling vs non-falling over word+particle); author notes Matsumori 2014/2015 posit three patterns and leaves the full accent system for future work; verbs contrast weakly.

tone_statements.quote: This paper attempts to show that the Japanese dialects in Haterumajima are tone-languages which have 2 types of pitch-pattern on their prosodical unit and are not pitch-accent languages like the Tokyo-dialect as they have been generally regarded. We can find out the same fact on the dialect of Shiraho hamlet in Ishigakijima-the hamlet known to have been settled by a forced immigration from Haterumajima in the 18th century.

tone.translation: Based on the above results, the accent system of the Funauki dialect can be described as follows. First, it has a unit, the prosodic word, above the syllable and below the bunsetsu, and for types b and c this unit functions as the counting unit. Second, the pitch movement specified by the accent type is realised with the syllable as its unit. Third, four accent types contrast by the presence/absence and position of a local pitch movement (rise). Table 6 outlines the Funauki system. The same interpretation can be adopted for Sonai and Hoshitate. For Amitori, since the kotei type is hardly attested, we interpret it as having a three-pattern accent system of types a, b, c.

tone.translation: First, as described in previous studies, simplex nouns distinguish two accent types (falling and flat). Second, in most compounds of two nouns the pitch pattern of the whole compound is determined by the accent type of the first member, i.e. the 'compound accent law' holds, though a few compounds show other patterns. Third, a regular correspondence is found: falling-type simplex nouns belong to Proto-Ryukyuan class A and flat-type nouns to classes B/C.

tone.translation: This paper compares the accent of the two dialects spoken in the northern and southern settlements of Hateruma Island and attempts a reconstruction of the Proto-Hateruma accent system of 2-mora and 3-mora nouns ['名調' sic for 名詞]. It further explains the process of change from the reconstructed proto-system to the accent systems of the northern- and southern-settlement dialects. The accent data for basic vocabulary are mainly taken from Hirayama & Nakamoto (1964), Hirayama, Oshima & Nakamoto (1967) and Sakimura (1987, 2006). Based on the regular correspondences between the northern and southern settlement accents, four types can be reconstructed for both 2-mora and 3-mora nouns in the proto-system.

tone.translation: In this way it became clear that the Kuroshima dialect too has a three-pattern accent system. ... (32) Mechanism of Kuroshima accent: (a) the accents of the three types in the system are distinguished by the presence or absence of a pitch fall and by its position. (b) The accent of each type appears as follows: type a, no fall; type b, in the second prosodic word (PW); type c, in the first prosodic word (PW). (c) The fall appears in principle on the penultimate mora of the respective PW. ... (33) Tone-assignment rules of Kuroshima: (a) H-tone rule: make high from the first mora of the prosodic phrase up to the accented mora. (b) L-tone rule: make low from the mora right after the accented mora to the last mora of the prosodic phrase.

tone.quote: 波照間方言は、ピッチの高低が弁別的な三型アクセント体系を有する。その 3 つとは、下降型、平進型、上昇型である。単一のアクセントがかかるドメインは、語、あるいは語と接語である。... 下降型：アクセント単位末尾に向けて下降する。... 平進型：下降も上昇もしない。... 上昇型：アクセント単位末尾に向けて上昇する。... 図に示す通り、アクセント単位の長さが変わってもアクセント型の対立が一定であり、上昇あるいは下降の位置、すなわちどの音節あるいはモーラでピッチが変動するかは、非弁別的である。そのため、N 型アクセント (上野 1977, 2012) でかつ語声調 (早田 1977, 1999) の言語であると言える。

tone.translation: The Hateruma dialect has a three-pattern accent system in which pitch height is distinctive. The three are the falling type, the level type and the rising type. The domain over which a single accent applies is the word, or the word plus clitic. ... Falling type: falls toward the end of the accent unit. ... Level type: neither falls nor rises. ... Rising type: rises toward the end of the accent unit. ... As the figures show, the opposition of accent types stays constant even when the length of the accent unit changes, and the position of the rise or fall, i.e. on which syllable or mora the pitch changes, is non-distinctive. It can therefore be said to be an N-pattern accent (Uwano 1977, 2012) and word-tone (Hayata 1977, 1999) language.

tone.translation: The Kuroshima dialect has two accent patterns. The first is a pattern with a fall at the end of the domain, the other a pattern with no fall. ... The domain to which the accent assignment rule applies is word + particle (the 'noun phrase with particle' of the next chapter). In the pattern containing a fall, the final mora within this domain becomes low. In the pattern without a fall, it is pronounced high to the end. ... Examples of each pattern follow. L means a low realisation, H a high realisation. (2-62) pattern with fall: /par/ HL 'needle', /pannudu/ LHHL 'needle-NOM'; pattern without fall: /tur/ LH 'bird', /tunnudu/ LHHH 'bird-NOM'.

tone.quote: Shiraho has a three-pattern pitch accent system that is determined lexically (Nakagawa and Celik 2019). The accent patterns are shown in figures 6.2, 6.3, and 6.4. Falling-1 is a steep falling pattern in which pitch falls around the second syllable. Falling-2 is a slightly falling pattern in which the pitch falls around the second syllable, but the degree of fall in pitch is lower than Falling-1. The level pattern keeps a high pitch. According to Nakagawa and Celik (2019), the falling-2 and level patterns are in complementary distribution ... In compound nouns, the tonal pattern is determined by that of the first constituent.
